title: Parallel, perpendicular and collinear
goal: I can use gradients to test for parallel lines, perpendicular lines and points on one line.
teach: Parallel lines have equal gradients: m₁ = m₂. Perpendicular lines have gradients that multiply to −1: m₁ × m₂ = −1, so flip the fraction and change the sign. Three points are collinear (on one straight line) if the gradients between them are equal.

ex.q: AB has A(0; 1) and B(2; 5). CD has C(1; 0) and D(5; −2). Are AB and CD perpendicular?
steps: mCD = −24 = −12.
2 × (−12) = −1, so AB ⊥ CD.

qs.text: Find k so that (0; 1), (2; 7) and (4; k) are collinear.
qs.steps:
1. Rule (collinear points): three points lie on one straight line if the gradient between the first two equals the gradient between the last two.
2. Gradient of the first two points: 7 − 12 − 0 = 3
3. k − 74 − 2 = 3, so k − 7 = 6
4. k = 13
